description: We are O.R.I.G.I.N, a team of students interested in space exploration, AI, data science, and technology. We want to use data to discover places on Earth that are similar to environments on the Moon and Mars. We are looking for teammates interested in space science, GIS, data analysis, programming, UI/UX, research, or storytelling.
summary: O.R.I.G.I.N (Orbital Reconnaissance & Intelligent Geo-analog Identification Network) is a web app that answers a practical question for mission planners and astronaut trainers: where on Earth can we train for a specific place on Mars or the Moon? The user picks a world and a location. O.R.I.G.I.N builds a physical profile of that site from NASA and USGS planetary maps, turns it into an Earth search target, and ranks Earth places with two tracks: terrain and climate measurements, and similarity of Sentinel-2 imagery embeddings from NASA/IBM’s Prithvi-EO-2.0 AI model. Each result shows a match score with confidence, the best Earth match for each characteristic, a 3D terrain view, and exactly where every number came from. A Compare mode tests any Mars or Moon place against any Earth place, feature by feature. It matters because analog sites are usually chosen by hand from documents, and fieldwork is expensive. O.R.I.G.I.N makes the comparison transparent, repeatable and open. Its Prithvi-based scoring was validated on Mars (AUC 0.91 vs 0.66 for a spectral baseline). We make no claim for the Moon, and the app is a prototype, not for mission planning.
details:
What it does and how it works

Choose: Mars or Moon, then a place. Coverage is 35 high-detail sites (8 validated benchmark sites and 27 coverage-only sites) and a coarse global profile (Mars 1,852 m/px, Moon 948 m/px) anywhere else. The page always shows which tier a result uses.

Profile: elevation, slope, thermal behaviour and albedo are read from NASA and USGS planetary maps.

Translate: the profile becomes an Earth search target (terrain ranges at the planetary map’s scale plus surface-type archetypes). Planetary images are never compared directly with Earth images.

Rank: Earth places are scored on terrain, geology, remoteness, logistics, climate and best training months from open data, plus Prithvi embedding similarity on Sentinel-2 patches. Candidates come from 41 precomputed Earth places.

Explain: a score with confidence, a top 5, the best match per characteristic, a 3D terrain view from real Copernicus DEM and Sentinel-2, and a “Where this came from” drawer (dataset, host, date, cached or live, file hash).

Benefits and intended impact: a faster, repeatable first screening for analog training sites, usable offline for the precomputed sites, with every number traceable. It supports education and early-stage planning. It does not replace field validation.

Tools: Python, FastAPI, PyTorch with Prithvi-EO-2.0-300M-TL (Hugging Face), CesiumJS and Three.js (plain ES modules, no build step), and a Kaggle T4 GPU for Prithvi embeddings. Parts of the code were written with Claude Code (AI-assisted development).

Creativity: it flips the usual question: instead of scoring an Earth site against fixed analogs, it starts from a Mars or Moon place and searches Earth. It adds a cinematic stage and per-characteristic best matches, and it shows honest “AI score / Real satellite data / Document reference / Experimental” badges on every number.

Factors we considered:

Validation: Mars AUC 0.91 [0.73–1.00] vs 0.66 [0.36–0.91] for a spectral baseline (7 analog groups, 8 hard negatives). Moon: no claim.

Limits: planetary class thresholds are unverified assumptions, and Apollo “analogs” are crew training sites.

Honesty: no fabricated values, and missing data is shown as “not available”.

Cost and access: the site works offline for precomputed places because the 1.3 GB model is only needed for new Earth places.
